meta.name: Washington DC (National Mall)
meta.scaleNote: game units per real metre; uniform, no compression
meta.originNote: centre of the play box: the north edge of the Mall at 12th St NW, just south of Constitution Ave
meta.axes: +X = east (toward the Capitol), -Z = north, +Y up. Matches the minimap (screen up = -Z), so the map is not mirrored.
meta.rotNote: All rot values are three.js rotation.y (radians). An object rotated by rot has its local +X axis pointing along (cos rot, -sin rot) in world (x, z). Building w is along local X, d along local Z.
meta.footprintNote: Footprints are CCW viewed from above (CCW in (x, -z)), open rings (first vertex not repeated). For THREE.Shape use (x, -z) then rotateX(-PI/2).
meta.heightNote: height / eaveHeight are game units (metres x 0.2). Landmarks: heightMetres = top of the structure incl. domes, statues, towers and spires; eaveMetres = main roof / cornice line; front = the side the main facade faces (the layout rot comes from the outline and is ambiguous by quarter turns). Buildings: heightSource says where each height came from.
meta.source: OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0 (https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright), Overpass API snapshot 2026-11-15: roads, water, parks, paths, bridges, building footprints, OSM height / building:levels / building:part heights, trees. Landmark heights and sizes: Architect of the Capitol, National Park Service, Smithsonian, GSA and Wikipedia figures, cross-checked against OSM height tags. Untagged building heights: median of tagged heights within 150 m, clamped by footprint size (heightSource). Google Maps was not consulted: the Chrome extension was not connected.

bridges.name: Arlington Memorial Bridge
bridges.desc: Neoclassical 1932 bridge of white-grey North Carolina granite over concrete arches: nine low segmental arches, the centre one a steel bascule span (fixed since 1961), carved eagle-and-fasces medallions on the spandrels, bronze-and-granite balustrades, gilded bronze equestrian groups (Valor, Sacrifice) at the Lincoln Memorial end. 655 m long, 18 m wide, leads from the Lincoln Memorial circle straight to Arlington Cemetery.

landmarks.name: United States Capitol
landmarks.desc: The white heart of the map at the east end of the Mall, on Capitol Hill about 27 m above the Mall lawn. 229 m long north-south: a central block with a shallow pedimented east portico of Corinthian columns, linked by narrow connectors to the Senate wing (north) and House wing (south), each with its own pedimented portico and long Corinthian colonnades. Walls of white Massachusetts marble and painted sandstone (warm off-white #EDE8DC), shallow grey-copper roofs hidden behind balustrades. Rising from the centre the cast-iron dome (painted white, 29 m wide): a colonnaded drum of 36 columns, a second ribbed attic drum with tall windows, the ribbed dome itself, a small colonnaded lantern and the bronze Statue of Freedom (dark bronze, 5.9 m) on top at 88 m. West side faces the Mall over the stepped West Front terraces (Olmsted terrace, two grand stairs, grey granite and white marble balustrades). The dome is the second-tallest thing on the map and should read from everywhere.

landmarks.name: Washington Monument
landmarks.desc: A plain tapering obelisk 169.3 m tall, 16.8 m square at the base narrowing to 10.5 m at 152 m, then a 17 m pyramidion to a small aluminium tip. White Maryland marble outer face over granite; a visible colour change about a third of the way up (150 ft) where construction resumed with slightly warmer-toned stone (lower #F2EFE8, upper #E9E1D2). Two small square observation windows on each face just below the pyramidion, tiny red aircraft lights at the top. Stands on a low grassy knoll ringed by 50 US flags on white poles (circle about 80 m across). The tallest structure on the map; nothing else comes close.

landmarks.name: Lincoln Memorial
landmarks.desc: A Greek Doric temple without a pediment, 61 x 40 m (long side north-south), 30 m tall. 36 fluted Doric columns of white Colorado Yule marble (#F3F1EC), 13.4 m tall, slightly tilted inward, ring the cella; a plain frieze with the 36 state names and an attic band with 48 state names and swags above. Flat roof (skylit). The open east face looks straight down the Reflecting Pool to the Monument and the Capitol; inside, the seated grey-white Georgia marble statue of Lincoln (5.8 m) between two inner colonnades. Sits on a high terraced podium: a 4 m granite retaining wall 57 x 78 m and wide grey granite and marble stairs falling east to the Reflecting Pool plaza, with the Watergate Steps toward the river behind.

landmarks.name: The White House
landmarks.desc: The Executive Residence: a white-painted Aquia sandstone Palladian mansion 51 x 26 m (long side east-west), three storeys over a ground floor that is only exposed on the south. North front (Pennsylvania Ave side): a pedimented Ionic portico of four columns over the carriage drive. South front (facing the Ellipse and the Monument): the semicircular South Portico, six tall Ionic columns rising the full height to a balcony (Truman Balcony). Low-pitch grey roof behind a balustrade, chimneys; American flag on the roof. Pure white (#F7F6F2) with dark green-black window sash. Low colonnaded terraces run west to the West Wing (two storeys, white, flat roof with the Oval Office bow on the south-east). The East Wing site is the new State Ballroom (construction, 2025-26). The lawns: the North Lawn with its fountain and the large oval South Lawn with its fountain, behind black iron fences.

landmarks.name: Thomas Jefferson Memorial
landmarks.desc: A round neoclassical pantheon on the south shore of the Tidal Basin, facing north across the water to the White House. A circular colonnade of 26 white Vermont Imperial Danby marble Ionic columns (#F4F2EC) 50 m across around an open-sided rotunda, under a shallow white marble dome rising to 39.6 m. A deep pedimented portico of eight columns (two rows) projects north with a sculpted pediment, reached by a broad flight of granite and marble stairs that step down to a plaza and the Basin seawall. Inside, the 5.8 m dark bronze standing statue of Jefferson. The memorial sits on a stepped circular podium; the shore around it is lined with Yoshino cherry trees (pale pink in bloom).

landmarks.name: Smithsonian Institution Building (The Castle)
landmarks.desc: A Norman-revival castle of deep red-purple Seneca sandstone (#8C3B34 to #9E4A3E), 137 m long east-west and about 40 m deep, facing north onto the Mall. A long two-storey central hall with round-arched windows and a steep dark slate roof, flanked by lower wings and end pavilions. Nine towers of different heights: on the north front a pair, the taller 44 m with a pointed slate spire; a tall 28 m square south tower; a slender octagonal campanile 36 m at the north-east corner; small turrets with pyramidal caps. Roofs dark grey slate, trim the same red stone. The formal Enid A. Haupt Garden (parterre lawn, flower beds) lies behind it to the south.

landmarks.name: National Museum of Natural History
landmarks.desc: A huge Beaux-Arts museum, 216 m east-west and 111 m deep (with the later north wings), of pale grey-white granite (#E3E0D8). The Mall (south) front: a central pavilion with a six-column Corinthian portico under a pediment, a broad stair, and behind it the green copper-clad octagonal rotunda dome (green #6E9A82 patina) rising to 38 m, with long three-storey wings either side ending in pavilions. Flat roofs behind a cornice; rows of tall windows. Faces the Castle across the Mall.

landmarks.name: National Air and Space Museum
landmarks.desc: A 1976 modernist block 209 x 69 m (long side east-west) facing the Mall: four large closed cubes clad in pink Tennessee marble (#D9B9A6) alternating with three tall glass-and-steel atrium bays (dark tinted glass, white steel frames) where aircraft hang. Flat roofs, a single 25 m height throughout. A glass restaurant pavilion at the east end. The 2018-26 renovation re-clad the cubes in the same pink stone. Low terraces and a bosque of trees between it and Jefferson Drive.

landmarks.name: National Gallery of Art, West Building
landmarks.desc: John Russell Pope's 1941 neoclassical gallery, 239 m long east-west, of rose-pink Tennessee marble (#E9D3C5, graded darker at the base). A windowless temple-like mass: the central block has an Ionic portico on the Mall side and on Constitution Ave, and above it a low saucer dome on a drum over the rotunda (dark green-grey roof) to 41 m. Long sculpture-hall wings with flat roofs and skylights, a plain attic band; end pavilions. Broad granite stairs to the Mall. Linked by an underground concourse to the East Building across 4th Street.

landmarks.name: National Gallery of Art, East Building
landmarks.desc: I. M. Pei's 1978 gallery on a trapezoid site where Pennsylvania Ave meets the Mall: two sharp triangles (an isoceles gallery triangle and a right-triangle study centre) joined, with knife-edge 19-degree corners. The same pink Tennessee marble as the West Building (#E5CDBE) in smooth flat walls almost without windows, three blocky towers rising to 33 m, a deep recessed entrance on the west facing the West Building, and a triangular glass space-frame skylight roof over the atrium. On the plaza in front: glass tetrahedron skylights (pyramids 1-5 m) and a fountain.

landmarks.name: National Museum of African American History and Culture
landmarks.desc: David Adjaye's 2016 museum at the Mall's north-west corner by the Monument: a three-tiered inverted stepped pyramid (the 'Corona') on a glass base, about 85 m square at the top, each tier flaring outward at 17 degrees. The corona is a screen of 3,600 cast-aluminium panels coated bronze (#8A5A36, warm burnished bronze with a lattice pattern), over a fully glazed recessed ground floor. A deep shaded 'Porch' canopy projects on the south (Mall) side over a reflecting pool. Five storeys above ground, about 31 m to the top of the corona. Dark and warm against the white marble around it.

landmarks.name: Hirshhorn Museum
landmarks.desc: Gordon Bunshaft's 1974 hollow concrete drum: a perfect cylinder 70 m across and 25 m tall, raised 4 m off the ground on four massive sculptural piers, with a 35 m open central courtyard and a bronze fountain. Smooth precast concrete of pink-grey granite aggregate (#C9BBAE), windowless except one long horizontal slot window on the third floor facing the Mall. The plaza around it is walled; the sunken Sculpture Garden lies across Jefferson Drive on the Mall side.

landmarks.name: National World War II Memorial
landmarks.desc: A sunken oval plaza 103 x 74 m (long axis east-west) at the east end of the Reflecting Pool, around the Rainbow Pool with its fountain jets. The plaza is paved in grey and pink granite and stepped down about 2 m. Ringing it, 56 granite pillars (5.2 m, grey-white Kershaw granite #D8D4CC) each with a bronze oak and wheat wreath, linked by a bronze rope, in two semicircles, and two 13 m pavilions (arches) on the north (Atlantic) and south (Pacific) ends with bronze eagles holding a laurel. On the west side the Freedom Wall of 4,048 gold stars. Ramps and lawn panels at the east entrance on 17th Street.

landmarks.name: National Archives Building
landmarks.desc: John Russell Pope's 1935 temple of archives on Constitution Ave: a 101 x 65 m block of Indiana limestone (#E2DACB) with a giant Corinthian colonnade on all sides, a pedimented portico of 8 columns on each main face (Constitution Ave south side faces the Mall, Pennsylvania Ave north side), and a tall plain stepped attic in the centre rising to 46 m. Green bronze doors, grand stairs on the Constitution side. Sits in Federal Triangle across from the Sculpture Garden.

landmarks.name: Old Post Office (Waldorf Astoria)
landmarks.desc: An 1899 Romanesque Revival post office on Pennsylvania Ave: a 9-storey granite block about 92 x 61 m of rough-faced grey-brown granite (#9C9384) with round arches, steep dark red-brown hip roofs, dormers and corner turrets. Its clock tower, centred on the Pennsylvania Ave (north) front (towerXZ), rises to 96 m: square, with arcaded bell openings, clock faces and a steep pyramidal roof with corner pinnacles. The third-tallest structure on the map; its dark mass stands out among the pale limestone of Federal Triangle.

landmarks.name: Treasury Building
landmarks.desc: The Greek Revival Treasury beside the White House on 15th St: a 142 x 76 m (long side north-south) block of granite painted/weathered pale grey-white (#E6E2D8) around two courtyards. A continuous colonnade of 30 Ionic columns along the 15th St (east) front, pedimented Ionic porticoes on the north and south ends (Alexander Hamilton statue on the south). Flat roof behind a balustrade, four storeys plus a basement.

landmarks.name: Supreme Court Building
landmarks.desc: Cass Gilbert's 1935 marble temple on 1st St NE facing the Capitol: a 117 x 92 m block in brilliant white Vermont marble (#F5F3EE) with four inner courtyards. The west front is a deep portico of 16 Corinthian columns (two rows) under a sculpted pediment ('Equal Justice Under Law') rising to 28 m, above a broad oval plaza with fountains, flagpoles and two seated marble figures beside a long flight of steps. Low-pitch grey-tan tile roof on the central block.

landmarks.name: Library of Congress, Thomas Jefferson Building
landmarks.desc: The 1897 Italian-Renaissance library across 1st St SE from the Capitol: a 143 x 104 m block of grey New Hampshire granite (#BDB7AC) with four corner pavilions and a projecting central west pavilion with paired columns and a grand stair (Court of Neptune fountain at its foot). Over the central octagonal reading room rises a copper dome gilded on its ribs and lantern (dark verdigris green #4F7466 with a bright gold flame-of-knowledge torch on top) to 59 m. Dark copper roofs, round windows on the attic.

landmarks.name: Eisenhower Executive Office Building
landmarks.desc: The 1888 Second Empire office palace west of the White House on 17th St: a 172 x 77 m block (long side north-south) of grey granite (#A9A59C) layered with tiers of free-standing columns (900 columns), five storeys of pedimented windows, and steep dark slate mansard roofs (#45474A) with dormers, cresting and many chimneys, pavilions at the corners and centres. Busier and darker than every other building nearby.

landmarks.name: National Museum of American History
landmarks.desc: A 1964 modernist block between 12th and 14th St on the Mall's north side, 177 x 88 m, clad in pinkish-grey Tennessee marble (#D8CBC0) in tall vertical panels with deep recessed slot windows and a projecting flat cornice slab; the upper storey is set behind a band of marble fins. Flat roof with skylights. A broad terrace on the Mall side; the steel Infinity sculpture at the 14th St corner.

landmarks.name: National Museum of the American Indian
landmarks.desc: A 2004 museum at the foot of Capitol Hill, a curving stratified mass of golden-buff Kasota limestone (#C9A86E) carved to look like wind-worn mesa cliffs, five storeys with rounded horizontal ledges and deep overhangs, a rounded glass-and-dome Potomac atrium facing east to the Capitol, prism windows. Set among wetland, meadow and boulder landscapes. Unlike every other museum here, no straight walls.

landmarks.name: Arts and Industries Building
landmarks.desc: An 1881 polychrome brick exhibition hall east of the Castle: a 99 m square Greek-cross plan of red and buff brick with blue and black patterned bands, a central octagonal rotunda with a raised clerestory and lantern, four gabled naves and corner pavilions with low towers, grey slate and metal roofs.

landmarks.name: Freer Gallery of Art
landmarks.desc: A 1923 Italian-Renaissance palazzo west of the Castle, 2 storeys of pale pink-grey granite (#D9D0C4) around a central courtyard, with an arcaded entrance loggia facing the Mall and a low flat roof behind a balustrade. About 69 x 69 m.

landmarks.name: US Botanic Garden Conservatory
landmarks.desc: A 1933 glass conservatory at the foot of the Capitol: a limestone front block with tall arched windows, and behind it a large glass-and-aluminium palm house with a tall barrel-vaulted central dome-house (24 m), plus lower glass wings, white frames on clear glass.

landmarks.name: US Holocaust Memorial Museum
landmarks.desc: A 1993 museum on 14th St SW of red-brown brick and grey limestone, with a curved limestone screen front on 14th St, steel and glass bridges and a row of brick towers with glass-topped lanterns along the north side.

landmarks.name: Bureau of Engraving and Printing
landmarks.desc: A 1914 classical industrial block of pale Indiana limestone with a long Doric colonnade on 14th St and five storeys of large factory windows; flat roof.

landmarks.name: Jamie L. Whitten Building (USDA)
landmarks.desc: The Department of Agriculture's Beaux-Arts headquarters on the Mall's south side: a long white marble central block with a Corinthian colonnade facing the Mall and two lower wings, flat roof, about 230 m long.

landmarks.name: USDA South Building
landmarks.desc: A huge 1936 office block of buff brick and limestone trim, seven wings like a comb between Independence Ave and the freeway, about 290 x 150 m. Plain and repetitive; linked to the Whitten Building by bridges over Independence.

landmarks.name: Ronald Reagan Building
landmarks.desc: A 1998 limestone giant of Federal Triangle: about 250 m long with a semicircular glass-roofed atrium, pale Indiana limestone (#E0D8C8), granite base, copper-green mansard tops and a tall glass rotunda entrance.

landmarks.name: Herbert C. Hoover Building (Commerce)
landmarks.desc: The 1932 Department of Commerce, a 312 m long Federal Triangle block of pale limestone with Doric colonnades, red tile hip roofs and six courtyards, along 15th St facing the Ellipse.

landmarks.name: EPA (William Jefferson Clinton Buildings)
landmarks.desc: The curving Federal Triangle complex around the Andrew W. Mellon Auditorium: neoclassical limestone with colonnades and red tile roofs, matching the rest of the Triangle.

landmarks.name: Internal Revenue Service Building
landmarks.desc: A 1930 Federal Triangle block on Constitution Ave between 10th and 12th St: limestone, Ionic pilasters, red tile hip roofs over a granite base.

landmarks.name: Robert F. Kennedy Department of Justice Building
landmarks.desc: A 1935 Art Deco classical block between 9th and 10th St: limestone with aluminium doors and trim, red tile roof, Ionic columns on Constitution Ave.

landmarks.name: J. Edgar Hoover Building (FBI)
landmarks.desc: A 1975 Brutalist fortress on Pennsylvania Ave: rough beige precast concrete with deeply recessed dark windows, seven storeys on Pennsylvania Ave rising to eleven at the back, overhanging upper floors and a central courtyard.

landmarks.name: Frances Perkins Building (Labor)
landmarks.desc: A 1975 modernist office block of white precast concrete over the I-395 tunnel by Constitution Ave, long horizontal ribbon windows, flat roof.

landmarks.name: Harry S Truman Building (State)
landmarks.desc: The State Department, a vast stripped-classical block of buff limestone in Foggy Bottom: eight storeys, flat roof, rows of square windows.

landmarks.name: Federal Reserve Eccles Building
landmarks.desc: A 1937 stripped-classical building of white Georgia marble on Constitution Ave: a symmetrical block with a central pavilion of square pillars and a bronze eagle, flat roof.

landmarks.name: Main Interior Building
landmarks.desc: A 1936 limestone office block between C and E St, a spine with six wings, stripped classical, flat roof.

landmarks.name: National Academy of Sciences
landmarks.desc: A 1924 white Georgia marble building on Constitution Ave with a copper roof, three storeys, set back behind a lawn and elm grove where the bronze Einstein Memorial sits.

landmarks.name: DAR Constitution Hall
landmarks.desc: A 1929 neoclassical concert hall of white Alabama limestone with an Ionic portico on 18th St and a low pitched roof.

landmarks.name: Organization of American States
landmarks.desc: The 1910 Pan American Union palace: white Georgia marble, Spanish-colonial and Beaux-Arts, three grand arched entrances on 17th St, red tile roof, garden with a reflecting pool behind.

landmarks.name: John F. Kennedy Center
landmarks.desc: A 1971 white marble box on the Potomac, 192 x 91 m, ringed by thin gold-painted steel columns holding a deep flat roof overhang; glass walls behind the colonnade on the river terrace (west). Plain white Carrara marble (#F2F0EA).

landmarks.name: Watergate Complex
landmarks.desc: Curving 1960s apartment and office blocks by the river, white concrete with deep scalloped balcony ledges (teeth-like railings), 12-14 storeys.

landmarks.name: Cannon House Office Building
landmarks.desc: A 1908 Beaux-Arts office building of white marble and limestone with a long Doric colonnade facing the Capitol across Independence Ave.

landmarks.name: Longworth House Office Building
landmarks.desc: A 1933 neoclassical white marble office building with an Ionic colonnade on Independence Ave.

landmarks.name: Rayburn House Office Building
landmarks.desc: A 1965 white marble stripped-classical block, very large and plain, with a central portico of square columns facing the Capitol.

landmarks.name: Russell Senate Office Building
landmarks.desc: A 1909 Beaux-Arts white marble office building with a long Doric colonnade on Constitution Ave.

landmarks.name: Dirksen Senate Office Building
landmarks.desc: A 1958 stripped-classical white marble office block with a central portico of square columns.

landmarks.name: Library of Congress, James Madison Building
landmarks.desc: A 1980 white marble modernist block with tall square piers on Independence Ave; flat roof, very long.

landmarks.name: Library of Congress, John Adams Building
landmarks.desc: A 1939 Art Deco block of white Georgia marble with green-tinted granite base, flat roof, bronze doors.

landmarks.name: Union Station
landmarks.desc: Daniel Burnham's 1907 Beaux-Arts station: white Vermont granite, a central triple-arched entrance pavilion with statues under a barrel-vaulted roof, long arcaded wings, facing Columbus Circle and the Capitol.

landmarks.name: US Institute of Peace
landmarks.desc: A 2011 building by Constitution Ave and 23rd St: limestone base under a sweeping white translucent glass roof of two dove-wing curves.

landmarks.name: Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial
landmarks.desc: The 9.1 m 'Stone of Hope', a white-pinkish granite block (#E2D6CB) with the carved figure of Dr King, standing forward of the two halves of the 'Mountain of Despair' entrance; behind it a 137 m curved crescent inscription wall of the same granite. Faces the Jefferson Memorial across the Tidal Basin.

landmarks.name: Dwight D. Eisenhower Memorial
landmarks.desc: A 2020 memorial: a 137 m stainless-steel woven tapestry (dark grey, showing Pointe du Hoc cliffs) hung between two 24 m limestone columns, with smaller columns, framing a plaza on Independence Ave with bronze statues.

landmarks.name: Ulysses S. Grant Memorial
landmarks.desc: At the foot of Capitol Hill facing the Mall: a 77 x 22 m white marble platform with a central 13 m pedestal and the bronze equestrian Grant (green-black patina), flanked by a cavalry group and an artillery group in bronze, bronze lions at the corners. Fronts the Capitol Reflecting Pool.

landmarks.name: Peace Monument
landmarks.desc: A 13 m white marble column-and-statue group (Grief and History) in the traffic circle at Pennsylvania Ave and 1st St.

landmarks.name: James A. Garfield Monument
landmarks.desc: A bronze standing Garfield on a round pink granite pedestal in the circle at Maryland Ave and 1st St SW.

landmarks.name: Korean War Veterans Memorial
landmarks.desc: A triangle of juniper bushes and granite strips with 19 stainless-steel soldier statues in ponchos (2.2 m) walking toward a US flag, a polished black granite mural wall, and a round Pool of Remembrance with a linden grove.

landmarks.name: Vietnam Veterans Memorial
landmarks.desc: Two 75 m walls of polished black granite in a shallow V cut into the lawn, rising to 3.1 m at the apex, one arm pointing at the Monument and one at the Lincoln Memorial.

landmarks.name: Franklin Delano Roosevelt Memorial
landmarks.desc: A long series of four open-air rooms of rough red-brown South Dakota granite walls (#9A6A55) with waterfalls and bronze statues, strung along the Tidal Basin's west shore under cherry trees.

landmarks.name: Albert Einstein Memorial
landmarks.desc: A bronze seated Einstein (3.7 m) on a white granite bench, on a circular dais of dark granite set with metal studs in the trees on Constitution Ave.

landmarks.name: US Navy Memorial
landmarks.desc: A round granite plaza on Pennsylvania Ave with a world-map pavement, fountain pools, ship masts and the bronze Lone Sailor.

landmarks.name: Sylvan Theater
landmarks.desc: An open-air stage on the Monument grounds below the knoll, a white canopy and backstage block facing a sloping lawn.

landmarks.name: Lockkeeper's House
landmarks.desc: A tiny 1835 stone cottage (rubble grey stone, wood shingle roof) at 17th St and Constitution, the last trace of the Washington City Canal.

landmarks.name: Zero Milestone
landmarks.desc: A 1.2 m granite marker post with a bronze compass rose at the north edge of the Ellipse.

landmarks.name: District of Columbia War Memorial
landmarks.desc: A small round Doric temple of white Vermont marble, 14 m tall, with a shallow dome, in the trees of West Potomac Park.

landmarks.name: Japanese Pagoda
landmarks.desc: A grey stone five-tier pagoda (1957 gift of Yokohama) on the rocks of the Tidal Basin's west shore, near the 1651 Japanese Lantern.

landmarks.name: Bartholdi Fountain
landmarks.desc: A 9 m cast-iron fountain painted soft white with three caryatids holding a basin, gas lamps on top, in a round pool in Bartholdi Park.

player.note: Rises from the middle of the Tidal Basin and wades north toward the Washington Monument and the Mall, the Jefferson Memorial behind it. rot = rotation.y that turns a +Z-forward model to face -Z (north).

ring.note: Title Match ring on the open ground between the Washington Monument and the Ellipse, straddling Constitution Ave between 15th and 17th St: the White House 123 u north up the Ellipse, the obelisk 57 u south (outside the mat), the WWII Memorial and the Reflecting Pool to the south-west, Federal Triangle (Commerce) to the east. It is the only place on the map where the full Chicago ring and mat (half 45.5) stand on open ground: clear = half-size of the largest axis-aligned square free of buildings and props (small structures removed, listed in removedSmallStructures). Confirmed by the lead (2026-11-15): the venue box is 106 x 100 u (the widest clear box here: DAR Hall east face x -166.4, Commerce west face x -59.2) (venueBox [minX, minZ, maxX, maxZ]), clear of every building; inVenueBox lists what stands in it. The Mall proper (between the Monument and the Capitol, see alternatives) is 52-57 u between museum fronts and cannot take the Chicago ring. Inside the box: lawns, the Ellipse south half, Constitution Ave, 15th and 17th St, and about 600 trees (dc_trees.json leaves out every tree within ringClearTrees).

alternatives.note: the Mall lawn between 12th and 14th St (NMAH / Whitten gap), on the Monument-Capitol axis; only 52-57 u between museum fronts, so a ring of about half 24 at most
the Mall between 3rd and 4th St (NGA East / NMAI gap), the Capitol 130 u east; same width limit

duel.note: VS Duel: the two kaiju face each other along the Mall axis about 290 u apart (findOpenSpawn searches 20 u round each).

soldier.note: Lone Soldier start: the Sylvan Theater lawn on the Monument grounds at the foot of the knoll, facing north toward the obelisk with the Mall opening to the east.
